scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8155: We cannot reach anything on Campus 1 from the rest
of the network this morning -- none of the 172.16.10.x / 172.16.20.x /
172.16.30.x machines answer from over here, while the Campus 1 people say
everything works inside their own building. So the break is whatever joins
Campus 1 to the rest, and operations already named it when we rang: "their
edge box has probably died again" -- the one called "router16". I won't
pretend to know what that is, but it is your box. Check it and bring
Campus 1 back today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router16 is up: it holds its OSPF adjacencies
  (the mswitch0 uplink and the router7 link are Full), it has dynamic routes, and
  it forwards Campus 1 traffic to the rest of the network. A Campus 1 host reaches
  a Campus 2 host (e.g. 10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss. The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a core-router
  outage that is not occurring (cf. kath4-router16-ospfd-down, where router16's
  ospfd IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router16 down, Campus 1
cut off -- is NOT reproducible: router16 is up with full OSPF neighbors (mswitch0
uplink and the router7 link in Full state), it has dynamic routes, and a Campus 1
host reaches Campus 2 (10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router16 is healthy and forwarding,
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces a Campus
1 -> off-campus path through router16, finds it working, checks router16's OSPF
neighbors and that it is forwarding, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds"
a dead core router -- restarting router16 or blaming it to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk ticket describes a complete loss of reachability to Campus 1 (172.16.10.0/24, 172.16.20.0/24, 172.16.30.0/24) from the rest of the network, and points to router16 as the suspected edge failure. Direct inspection of every component in the path shows the network is fully healthy.

Router16 is operational: its bond0 interface (eth0+eth1 bonded, 10.2.2.1/24) is UP and carrying traffic toward mswitch0, and its eth2 (172.30.1.1/24) is UP toward router7. OSPF is converged on both links — router16 holds Full adjacencies to both mswitch0 (neighbor 172.16.30.254 via bond0, Full/Backup) and router7 (neighbor 192.168.10.1 via eth2, Full/DR). mswitch0 is also in Full state toward router16.

The Campus 1 VLAN gateways (vlan10 172.16.10.254, vlan20 172.16.20.254, vlan30 172.16.30.254) on mswitch0 are up and advertising their prefixes into OSPF. All WAN routers — router7, router1, and router17 — carry correct OSPF routes to the three 172.16.x.x /24s via 172.30.1.1 (router16). End-to-end pings from router1, router7, and router17 to real Campus 1 hosts (172.16.10.5, 172.16.20.254, 172.16.30.12) all return 0% packet loss. Campus 1 PCs can equally reach the WAN side (tested pc5→10.0.0.2 and pc12→192.168.10.2 with full success). No iptables rules or route black-holes exist on any device in the path.

Root cause: there is no fault — the ticket's premise is incorrect; Campus 1 is fully reachable from all parts of the network right now.

No corrective action is needed. The operations team should verify their own test methodology; the reported outage may have been a transient issue that self-resolved before this investigation, or the test was performed from a host with a misconfigured default gateway on the caller's side.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly verifies router16 is up with Full OSPF adjacencies and that end-to-end pings to Campus 1 hosts show 0% loss, confirming baseline health.

The agent's investigation ran appropriate control-plane and data-plane checks (OSPF neighbor states, routing tables, pings, iptables) and the observations in the log support the writeup's conclusion that router16 and Campus 1 are reachable. The inferences follow logically and the key alternative causes were effectively ruled out.
